questions.question: 33706. For taking primary impression of a patient with cleft palate, the material of choice is:
questions.explain:
Material           Usefulness for cleft palate primary impression:
Alginate-Flexible, flows well, safe in undercuts.
Silicone-Overly precise, costlier — good for final, not for primary impression
Impression compound - Rigid, can’t handle deep undercuts safely
Gutta-percha- Not an impression material at all.Soft, easy-flowing, records undercuts gently without trauma.

["Commonly used materials for cleft palate for impression are
Alginate, elastomer(silicone), impression compound(low fusing-green stick compound)." - Deepak 2nd edition
In case of 2stage method impression recording, 1st impression is taken by Green stick compound theb 2nd impression is taken by silicon.
When,undercut is needed for better retention in fabricating the Prosthesis, usually alginate is preferred. Choosing the materials  depends on the Clinical evaluation of the patient. 
So, keeping the question in mind, Alginate could be most preferable ans.As it is economical,flexible, and  records the undercut well.]

questions.question: 33696. Which syndrome associated with missing teeth:
questions.explain:
Gardner Syndrome: Gardner Syndrome is a variant of Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP) — a genetic disorder with:
• Hundreds of intestinal polyps (high cancer risk)
• Multiple osteomas of the jaws
• Odontomas(benign tooth-like growths)
• Supernumerary teeth (extra teeth) — not missing teeth
• Impacted teeth are common due to jaw osteomas and odontomas.

Gardner syndrome is more commonly associated with extra teeth and impacted teeth, not congenital absence (hypodontia).
Down Syndrome :Down Syndrome(Trisomy 21) has classic oral features:
• Hypodontia (missing teeth)— common
• Microdontia (small teeth)
• Delayed eruption
• Malocclusion
• Macroglossia (large tongue)

questions.question: 33695. An epithelial origin tumor is:
questions.explain: Most common oral cancer — arises from oral epithelium. Lipoma and fibroma are connective tissue tumors.

questions.question: 33694. Apex locator is helpful in patient with which of the following?
questions.explain: Helps locate length even for canals that are calcified, missed or hard to locate radiographically.

questions.question: 33693. Treatment objective of class II Div I malocclusion is:
questions.option4: Reduction of over jet and overbite
questions.explain: Class II Div I = protrusive upper incisors. Goal is to retract incisors and reduce excessive overjet.

questions.question: 33692. The maxillo-mandibular relationship is expressed in:
questions.explain: ANB: shows the relative forward/backward position of maxilla vs mandible. Used to diagnose skeletal Class I, II, III.

questions.question: 33691. A patient aged 8 years with skeletal anterior open bite is treated with:
questions.option2: Frankel appliance with high pull head gear
questions.option3: Posterior osteotomy to reposition posterior segment
questions.explain: This controls excessive vertical maxillary growth and helps close open bite in growing children.

questions.question: 33690. The most common site of ameloblastoma is:
questions.explain: Benign but locally aggressive tumor — 80% occur in posterior mandible, often associated with impacted third molars.

questions.question: 33689. Duplication model can be done by:
questions.explain: Same as before — reversible hydrocolloid for precise duplicating.

questions.question: 33688. Impacted teeth leaving in position instead of extraction:
questions.option1: When risk is greater than the potential benefit in older patient
questions.option2: For the prevention of periodontal disease
questions.option4: For the prevention of alveolar ostetis
questions.explain: In elderly, surgical removal may cause jaw fracture, nerve damage, osteomyelitis.If asymptomatic, it is better left alone.

questions.question: 33687. Causes of pain during the progression of pulp inflammation is due to:
questions.option1: Elevation of the sensory nerve threshold
questions.explain: Inflammation → vasodilation, fluid leakage → pressure inside rigid pulp chamber rises → severe pain.

questions.question: 33686. Dens invaginatus most commonly found in:
questions.explain: Enamel folds inward during development → invagination — often affects maxillary lateral incisors.

questions.question: 33685. Vasoconstrictor used in local anesthesia is:
questions.explain: Most common vasoconstrictor in dental LA — prolongs action, reduces bleeding, slows systemic absorption.

questions.question: 33684. Dentigerous cyst is:
questions.option1: Associated with dilatation of dental follicles
questions.option3: Developed from breakdown of stellate reticulum cells
questions.explain: Forms around the crown of an unerupted tooth, due to fluid accumulation between crown and reduced enamel epithelium.

questions.question: 33683. A balanced diet is one which contains:
questions.option4: All nutritive value in proper proportion
questions.explain: Balanced diet means right amounts of carbs, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and water for body needs.

questions.question: 33682. The burden of ill health of the community is:
questions.explain: Morbidity = disease prevalence/incidence → shows community’s health burden beyond just deaths (mortality)

questions.question: 33681. True LeFort II fracture includes:
questions.explain: Le Fort II: involves nasal bridge, lacrimal bone, orbital floor and rim — pyramidal fracture.

questions.question: 33680. The routine investigation for GA fitness includes:
questions.explain: Chest X-ray checks for lung health, TB, infections — essential before giving general anesthesia.

questions.question: 33679. Complication of surgical extraction of impacted mandibular third molar teeth is:
questions.option3: Displacement of root in infratemporal fossa
questions.explain: Inferior alveolar nerve runs close to third molar roots; surgical trauma can cause numbness or tingling in the lower lip.

questions.question: 33678. Radix entomolaris is an extra:
questions.option2: Distal root on the lingual aspect
questions.option3: Lingual root on the buccal aspect
questions.explain: It’s an additional third root found lingually on mandibular molars — common in certain populations (e.g., Mongoloid traits).

questions.question: 33677. Acute deficiency of which vitamin is responsible for tooth mobilization and gingival swelling?
questions.explain: Scurvy causes swollen, bleeding gums and loose teeth due to weakened collagen in the periodontal ligament.

questions.question: 33676. Most common reason for high caries incidence in children of higher income group is:
questions.option3: Repeated consumption of sticky refined sugar
questions.explain: Children with access to chocolates, sweets, sugary snacks have more frequent sugar exposure, leading to more caries, despite good brushing.

questions.question: 33674. Secondary stress bearing area of lower denture is:
questions.explain:
See the box of Q-121

Primary stress bearing for lower denture: buccal shelf area — strong cortical bone.

Secondary: the residual alveolar ridge, less ideal due to resorption and less resistance to load.

questions.question: 33673. Pus from from third molar infection may not track into:
questions.explain:
Pus commonly spreads to:
· Buccal space
· Lateral pharyngeal space
· Submandibular space
The peritonsillar space is not typically involved from a third molar infection.

questions.question: 33670. In LeFort II fracture of the maxilla the fracture line includes all except:
questions.explain: Le Fort II is a pyramidal fracture: involves nasal bridge, maxilla, orbital rim, orbital floor — but not the alveolar ridge specifically (that’s Le Fort I).

questions.question: 33669. Which following material is used for diagnostic impression material:
questions.explain: Alginate is an irreversible hydrocolloid — quick-setting, cheap, and gives sufficient detail for diagnostic casts (study models) but not for final crown work.

questions.question: 33668. The posterior teeth are set edge to edge without horizontal overjet; the possible discomfort may be:
questions.explain: Without horizontal overlap (overjet), the buccal cusps contact directly edge-to-edge. This can trap and bite the cheek tissue during mastication. Speech aberration also felt.

questions.question: 33667. Material used for model duplication is:
questions.explain: Agar is a reversible hydrocolloid — when heated, it liquefies; when cooled, it gels again. It’s ideal for duplicating cast models with fine details.

questions.question: 33666. Which of the following one tells about maxilla-mandibular relationship?
questions.explain:
ANB angle shows the anteroposterior relationship:
· A point (maxilla)
· B point (mandible)
· Nasion (reference)
ANB helps diagnose skeletal Class I, II, III.

questions.question: 33665. Basal arch length in normal dentition is almost equal in:
questions.explain: In well-aligned Class I occlusion, the basal bone (jaw) length and the dental arch length are harmoniously matched. In Class II or III, there’s disproportion due to jaw discrepancies.

questions.question: 33664. Von Korff's fibers are present in:
questions.explain: Von Korff’s fibers are thick collagenous fibers originating from odontoblasts. They extend into the dentin and help in the formation of mantle dentin — the first-formed outer layer of dentin.

questions.question: 33663. Deficiency of which vitamin causes delayed wound healing?
questions.explain: Vitamin C is vital for collagen synthesis, which is key for wound repair. Deficiency leads to poor fibroblast function, fragile capillaries and delayed healing — classic in scurvy.
